module.purpose: Provides React Flow utilities for applying node and edge changes, generating selection changes, and diffing element collections against the store.
module.summary: This module implements ordered change reconciliation for flow elements. It batches additions separately, collapses removals and replacements, applies sequential mutable updates to shallow-cloned elements, and preserves unchanged object references. It also provides selection-state helpers and computes add, remove, and replace operations by comparing incoming elements with lookup-backed store state.
module.businessContext: Supports interactive graph editing in React Flow, including dragging, selection, resizing, insertion, replacement, and deletion. Failure would leave the visual flow state inconsistent with user actions or the store.
functions: applyChanges (~L19-104): Applies ordered additions, removals, replacements, and updates generically
applyChange (~L107-149): Mutates one element according to a single change
applyNodeChanges (~L179-184): Applies typed changes to an array of nodes
applyEdgeChanges (~L214-219): Applies typed changes to an array of edges
createSelectionChange (~L221-228): Creates a selection-state change for one element
getSelectionChanges (~L230-256): Computes selection changes for mapped items and selected identifiers
getElementsDiffChanges (~L266-312): Computes additions, removals, and replacements against store lookup
elementToRemoveChange (~L314-319): Creates a removal change for one node or edge

mutationOfArg: applyChange mutates the supplied element object.
getSelectionChanges mutates mapped items when mutateItem is true.

moduleContractTests.scenario: An element receives multiple non-terminal changes in sequence.
given: const elements = [{ id: 'n1', position: { x: 0, y: 0 } }]
const changes = [{ id: 'n1', type: 'position', position: { x: 10, y: 20 } }, { id: 'n1', type: 'select', selected: true }]
moduleContractTests.then: the result contains one element with position { x: 10, y: 20 } and selected === true
moduleContractTests.rationale: Sequential changes must be applied cumulatively to a copied element.

moduleContractTests.scenario: A remove change targets an existing element.
moduleContractTests.then: the result is an empty array
moduleContractTests.rationale: Remove changes must omit the targeted element.

moduleContractTests.scenario: An add change specifies an insertion index.
given: const changes = [{ type: 'add', item: { id: 'n2' }, index: 1 }]
moduleContractTests.rationale: Added items must be inserted at their requested array index.

moduleContractTests.scenario: A selection state is requested for an element.
moduleContractTests.then: the result equals { id: 'n1', type: 'select', selected: true }
moduleContractTests.rationale: The returned change is the selection wire shape consumed by change application.

moduleContractTests.scenario: The next elements differ from the current lookup by identity, presence, and membership.
given: const lookup = new Map([['n1', { id: 'n1' }], ['n3', { id: 'n3' }]])
moduleContractTests.then: the result contains a replace change for n1, an add change for n2 at index 1, and a remove change for n3
moduleContractTests.rationale: Diff output must represent replacement, insertion, and deletion against the current lookup.

moduleContractTests.scenario: An existing node or edge is converted to a removal change.
moduleContractTests.rationale: Removal conversion must preserve the element identifier and use the remove discriminator.

detail.name: applyChanges
detail.signature: function applyChanges(changes: any[], elements: any[]): any[]
preconditions: changes is an iterable array of change objects.
elements is an iterable array of elements with an id property when changes target existing elements.
postconditions: Returns a new array containing the resulting elements.
Elements without queued changes are retained by reference and in their original order.
Removed elements are absent from the result.
Replacement items are shallow-copied into the result.
Added items are shallow-copied and inserted at their specified indices or appended when no index is specified.
Non-add changes for each element are applied in their queued order through applyChange.
invariants: Add changes are processed after all existing elements have been processed.
A remove or replace change supersedes changes previously queued for the same element.
When the first queued change for an element is remove, that element is omitted.
When the first queued change for an element is replace, the replacement item is used without applying subsequent queued changes.
edgeCases: An empty changes array returns the original elements in a new result array with the same element references.
An empty elements array returns shallow copies of added items, inserted or appended according to their indices.
A change with type add and no index appends its item.
A change with type add and an index inserts its item using array splice semantics; multiple additions are applied sequentially in change order.
Multiple changes targeting one element are accumulated and applied in input order unless an earlier remove or replace determines the result path.
A remove change causes the matching element to be omitted.
A replace change causes the matching element to be replaced by a shallow copy of its item.
Changes targeting an id not present in elements do not create an element unless they are add changes.
Malformed values that do not provide the properties needed during iteration or delegation may cause the underlying JavaScript operation or applyChange call to throw.

raises: Propagates runtime TypeError or other errors caused by invalid non-array inputs, malformed change objects, or failures from applyChange.
errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: No explicit validation or recovery is performed; runtime errors propagate.

stateMutations: Mutates only local arrays, maps, and shallow-copied element objects created during execution.
Does not mutate the input changes array or the input elements array.
Delegated applyChange operations mutate the per-element shallow copy, not the original element.
detail.summary: Applies a sequence of element changes to an input element array and returns the resulting array. Existing elements are updated, removed, or replaced according to their queued changes, while added items are inserted at requested indices or appended.

specLiterals.role: Identifies a change that inserts a shallow copy of an item.
Identifies a change that removes the element with the matching id.
Identifies a change that replaces the matching element with a shallow copy of an item.

specTests.then: The returned array contains only the original element with id "b"; the input elements array is not modified.

detail.name: applyChange
detail.signature: function applyChange(change: any, element: any): any
preconditions: change and element are supplied as mutable values compatible with the requested property assignments.
postconditions: For a select change, element.selected equals change.selected.
For a position change, defined position and dragging fields are copied to the corresponding element properties.
For a dimensions change, defined dimensions are shallow-copied into element.measured; selected width and height attributes are updated when requested, and a boolean resizing value is copied.
The function returns undefined.
invariants: Properties not targeted by the change type or its defined fields are left unchanged.
The dimensions object assigned to element.measured is a new shallow copy rather than the original change.dimensions object.
edgeCases: An unsupported or missing change.type results in no mutation and no thrown error.
A position change with an undefined position or dragging field leaves that corresponding element property unchanged.
A dimensions change with undefined dimensions skips measured, width, and height updates but may still update resizing when it is boolean.
A dimensions change updates width and/or height only when setAttributes is true, 'width', or 'height'; other truthy values do not update either attribute.
A dimensions change with a non-boolean resizing value leaves element.resizing unchanged.
A select change assigns change.selected directly, including when that value is undefined.

errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: Unsupported change types are ignored without throwing; otherwise property-access or assignment errors from incompatible inputs are not intercepted.

stateMutations: Mutates the supplied element.selected property for select changes.
Mutates the supplied element.position and element.dragging properties for defined position-change fields.
Mutates the supplied element.measured, element.width, element.height, and element.resizing properties according to dimensions-change fields.
detail.summary: Applies a supported change object directly to an element by mutating the relevant element properties. Unsupported change types produce no mutation.

specLiterals.role: Change type that updates the element selection state.
Change type that updates position and dragging state.
Change type that updates measured dimensions and resizing state.
setAttributes value selecting width attribute propagation.
setAttributes value selecting height attribute propagation.

specTests.when: applyChange is called with the change and element.
specTests.then: The element position is replaced with the supplied position, while the existing dragging and unrelated properties remain unchanged.
element.measured is a shallow copy of the dimensions, element.width becomes 100, and element.height is not updated by this change.

units.name: applyEdgeChanges
units.source:
*```
 * @remarks Various events on the <ReactFlow /> component can produce an {@link EdgeChange}
 * that describes how to update the edges of your flow in some way.
 * If you don't need any custom behaviour, this util can be used to take an array
 * of these changes and apply them to your edges.
 */

detail.name: applyEdgeChanges
detail.signature: export function applyEdgeChanges<EdgeType extends Edge = Edge>(changes: EdgeChange<EdgeType>[], edges: EdgeType[]): EdgeType[]
preconditions: The changes argument is an array of valid EdgeChange<EdgeType> values.
The edges argument is an array of EdgeType values.
Edge identifiers used by changes correspond to the identifier field expected by EdgeChange.
postconditions: The returned array reflects the supplied changes in their input order.
The returned value has type EdgeType[].
The input edges array is not replaced in place.
invariants: Edge identity is determined by edge id.
Unchanged edges retain their existing values and ordering.
edgeCases: An empty changes array yields an edge array equivalent to the input edges.
A change targeting an edge id that is not present has no effect.
Add, remove, replacement, and selection changes are handled according to the EdgeChange discriminant and preserve the resulting edge ordering defined by the shared change application utility.
detail.summary: Applies an ordered collection of edge changes to an existing edge array. It returns the resulting edges while preserving the edge-specific generic type.

specTests.when: applyEdgeChanges is called with that change and the edge array
specTests.then: The returned array contains the same edges with edge "b" updated to the requested selection state.
The targeted edge is absent from the returned array and the other edges remain.
The new edge is included in the returned array according to the shared change-application ordering.
